comment: Every test failure this repository currently expects, and why.
It exists because a step that is already red absorbs the next failure without trace.
TestGenerateCatalogIdempotent was red on main for two merges, inside a step red for the
ratchet; TestFirehoseSnowflakeSecretAndPersistentBuffer failed once inside the same step
and was invisible for the same reason. Neither was hidden cleverly. Both were hidden by a
scripts/known-red.sh reads a `go test` run and says which of its failures are on this list
and which are not. It does NOT make anything pass: every entry here is still a red test and
still fails its step. What changes is that the first line of the output says whether the red
is the one expected or a new one -- which is the whole difference between a gate and a colour.
An entry may be added only with a reason a reader can check, and removed the moment the test
goes green. TestKnownRedIsDeclaredHonestly enforces both halves: every entry must name a test
that exists in the tree and carry a non-empty reason.

expected.why: Deliberate, and the point of the ratchet. The baseline is the PRE-DRIFT target, not a floor to raise: one pack -- azure/blobs -- is still in the tree after it was cut, so the tree exceeds it until that pack is extracted. It was two until railway/graphql went, which is what moved every count here down. Goes green by deleting the pack, never by running `ratchet -write`.

The other half of the same statement: ratchet.json is deliberately stale relative to the tree, for exactly as long as TestRatchetNotExceeded is red, and now for the one remaining pack rather than two.

Red for ONE service: azure.blobs, the hand-written pack still to be extracted. The other three served without a generated model (aws.elastictranscoder, aws.lookoutmetrics, aws.qldb) do not make it red -- the test allows exactly the services specs/aws-dirs.json records in its "unavailable" map, which it now reads rather than transcribes. AWS publishes no model for those three in api-models-aws at all, so there is nothing for a receiver to ingest and no work that makes them go away; this entry used to say the receiver could not ingest them, which sent a reader after a bug that does not exist. Goes green when azure.blobs is extracted, and not before. It was five services until railway.graphql got a model of its own -- a GraphQL receiver, its schema fetched by POSTing an introspection query and pinned like any other vendored document. The count may only fall.
